news.title: Uefa preparing to bring criminal claims against Gianni Infantino over World Cup sale
news.lede: Uefa says claims will be made in Switzerland. It says claims relate to alleged criminal mismanagement. Uefa is preparing to make a criminal complaint against Gianni Infantino for alleged “criminal mismanagement” in connection with his failed Fifa Forward Enterprise plan and has applied for the release of documents related to its conception. In an explosive escalation of the war engulfing football’s governing bodies, Uefa has made separate applications in the United States for information, including from Fifa.

news.title: Infantino doing ‘great job’ World Cup star Suker says, tells Hong Kong ‘be more like Croatia’
news.lede: Soon after he joined the Hong Kong football association 2½ years ago, the now outgoing technical director John Morling pointed to the success of Croatia and asked, “why can’t that be us?” With a population just shy of 4 million, Croatia have reached one World Cup final and two semi-finals in the past 28 years. Now, Davor Suker, one of the stars of their 1998 run to the last four, is poised to share some of his country’s secrets with Hong Kong: population 7 million, world No 156 and as far away as ever from qualifying for a World Cup, even if it is expanded to 64 teams. The former Real Madrid and Arsenal striker, who is a Fifa ambassador and leapt to the defence of president Gianni Infantino on Thursday, Suker has been made honorary president of Hong Kong Premier League club Eastern District.

news.title: AIFF confirms date as India set to face two-time World Cup champions Uruguay
news.lede: India will face two-time FIFA World Cup winners Uruguay in a major international friendly on October 6 at the Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan in Kolkata.The match will be part of a busy FIFA window for India, with the team set to play three strong opponents in just 11 days.India set for major World Cup testsIndia will first meet Panama in Bengaluru on September 26 before taking on five-time world champions Brazil in Kolkata on October 3. Uruguay, currently ranked 20th in the world, will then arrive for the final match on October 6. Uruguay have won the World Cup twice, lifting the trophy in 1930 and 1950. Their visit gives Indian players another chance to test themselves against experienced international opposition.The Uruguay match will come only three days after Brazil's visit, making Kolkata the main football venue during the window.

news.title: India to take on two-time World champions Uruguay in high-profile football friendly on October 6
news.lede: India are set to host two-time FIFA World Cup winners Uruguay in a high-profile international friendly at the Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan, Kolkata, on October 6. The Uruguay game will be India's third marquee friendly during the upcoming FIFA window. The national side will first take on Panama in Bengaluru on September 26 before meeting five-time world champions Brazil in Kolkata on October 3. Uruguay's visit will give Indian football fans the opportunity to watch another established World Cup nation in the space of a few days.

news.title: India to face two-time FIFA World Cup winner Uruguay after Brazil clash in Kolkata
news.lede: India's already packed international window has gained another major fixture, with Uruguay confirmed as their next high-profile opponent in Kolkata. The All India Football Federation announced that the two-time FIFA World Cup champions will face India on October 6 at the Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan.The announcement comes as the attention around India's upcoming friendlies continues to grow, particularly with Brazil's much-awaited visit to Kolkata. India will first take on Panama in Bengaluru on September 26 before facing Brazil at the Salt Lake Stadium on October 3 and then Uruguay three days later.Uruguay remain one of the biggest names in world football despite a disappointing campaign at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
